findings.title: Trailing \b defeats stem patterns in classifyFindingRisk, so breaking/compat lenses are misclassified as substantive
findings.summary: The lensIsBreaking regex ends every alternative with \b, but three alternatives are word STEMS (compat, deprecat, remov); a stem followed by any letter (compatibility, deprecated, removal) fails the trailing word-boundary and the whole alternation backtracks to no-match, so those lenses fall through to the substantive tier instead of context_dependent.
findings.impact: A finding whose lens signals a breaking/compat concern (e.g. "compatibility" or "removal" in a free-form auditor report) is classified substantive instead of context_dependent and is routed straight to dispatch instead of through the context-dependent review tier, applying a risky change without the intended human review.
evidence: Regex semantics: \b after "remov" requires a non-word character next, but the intended inputs are words like "removal"/"deprecated"/"compatibility", whose next character is a letter, so the boundary assertion fails and the alternative is rejected.
Only whole-word alternatives (interface, breaking, api-break) can ever match; the three stem alternatives are unreachable against any natural-language lens string.

findings.title: uniqueSortedEdges orders with localeCompare, making edge order locale-dependent instead of content-derived
findings.summary: The final sort in uniqueSortedEdges compares endpoints with localeCompare and no locale argument, so the emitted edge order depends on the host's default ICU locale rather than content; the same graph content can serialize in a different order on a different machine or ICU build, breaking the byte-identical/content-derived-order property this module's own documentation claims and churning artifact content hashes downstream.
findings.impact: Cross-environment runs over an identical tree can produce differently ordered graphs arrays; since stableStringify preserves array order, the persisted graph artifact's content hash changes, cascading phantom staleness down the dependency DAG and triggering redundant expensive downstream re-runs. Orderings diverge specifically for paths where collation variable-weighting applies (punctuation such as '-', '.', '/' at segment boundaries), which is common in repo paths.
evidence: Sort comparator is a.from.localeCompare(b.from) || a.to.localeCompare(b.to) || (a.kind ?? "").localeCompare(b.kind ?? "") with no explicit locale or sensitivity, unlike the dedupe half of the same function which uses stableStringify comparison precisely to stay content-derived.

The function's doc comment claims 'a shuffled input array yields byte-identical output', which holds only for a fixed host locale; ECMA-402 leaves default-locale collation implementation- and ICU-version-dependent.
Repo invariant ('Extractors emit stable, content-derived array order') requires order derived from content, never environment; codepoint comparison (a < b) would satisfy it.

findings.summary: getFlag/setFlag locate options by exact token equality with '--root'/'--artifacts-dir', so an equals-form argument like --root=./sub is never seen: runDistCommand resolves rootValue from '.' instead and setFlag APPENDS a second --root pointing at the caller's cwd, leaving the dist CLI with two conflicting values where the caller's explicit one can lose.
findings.impact: Invoking 'node audit-code.mjs next-step --root=./target' silently audits the package/caller directory instead of ./target and writes artifacts beside the wrong tree, with no error naming the discarded value.
evidence: getFlag (lines 48-52) and setFlag (lines 59-66) both use argv.indexOf(name) with name equal to the bare '--root' / '--artifacts-dir' tokens; neither matches the '--root=X' spelling.

runDistCommand (lines 219-227) therefore computes rootValue = resolve('.') and then setFlag pushes '--root <abs-cwd>' onto commandArgs because the equals-form token was not found, producing an argv that carries BOTH '--root=./sub' and '--root /abs/cwd'.
The same applies to --artifacts-dir, so a caller's explicit artifacts directory is likewise shadowed by the derived default.

This is the same failure class the CE-001 comment on lines 54-58 documents for fill-only-if-missing defaults: a caller-supplied relative root must be normalized, not replaced — but the equals form slips past recognition entirely and the appended value overrides it (commander-style parsers take the last occurrence of a non-variadic option).

findings.title: computeCriticalPathMs double-counts the shared job when the needs graph has a cycle
findings.summary: On a cycle, walk() detects the revisit and returns only the revisited job's own duration (discarding nothing, memoizing nothing), and every caller on the cycle then adds its own duration on top - so a job on a dependency cycle is counted once extra per cycle member, inflating the reported critical path.
findings.impact: With A needing B and B needing A (durations a, b), walk(B) returns a, so B totals b+a and is memoized; walk(A) then totals a+(b+a) = 2a+b, overstating the true cycle cost max(a,b)+min path by a full extra pass over the cycle. Output lands in writeProfileLedger('publish-ci', ...) criticalPathMs, so release-timing baselines can be silently wrong. Latent today because GitHub Actions rejects cyclic needs, but the function is written defensively for exactly that input and gets it wrong.

findings.title: Coverage contract forces reviewed_lines == total_lines, making partial review indistinguishable from full review
findings.summary: The audit result-ingest validator refuses any file_coverage entry whose reviewed_lines differs from total_lines (src/audit/cli/dispatch/hostHandoff.ts:906-915: 'must report reviewed_lines equal to total_lines'), and separately pins each path's total_lines to the binding's file_line_counts (:916-925) and requires exact scope coverage (:927-934). The composite effect is that the ONLY acceptable submission asserts complete review of every bound file, so the field carries zero information: a host that skimmed or skipped a file must either submit a false equality or fail ingestion entirely, and the tool cannot tell a genuine full pass from a coerced one. The contract therefore records an attestation it cannot verify and simultaneously forbids the honest intermediate states (partial review, reviewed-with-follow-up) that a bounded host context makes likely on large bound files. Observational recommendation, not a redesign: either drop reviewed_lines (it is derivable — it always equals the bound total) and keep the explicit full-coverage attestation in the prompt text, or widen the contract to accept a reported reviewed_lines below the bound as a classified partial-coverage outcome the orchestrator can act on, so the machine contract stops encoding 'full review' as the only representable fact.

findings.title: dedupeTasks suite cannot detect in-place mutation or identity return
findings.summary: Every case compares the returned array's content against the same tasks literal it passed in, so an implementation that sorts, splices, or filters the caller's array in place and returns it would pass the entire suite; nothing asserts the input array is left untouched or that the result is a distinct array.

findings.title: Failed lock-file write inside acquireBuildLock orphans the build lock for up to 5 minutes

findings.title: getFlag takes the next token blindly, so a value-less --root/--artifacts-dir silently normalizes to a bogus absolute path and mkdirs a directory named after the flag
findings.summary: getFlag returns argv[index + 1] without checking it is a value, so `next-step --root --artifacts-dir /tmp/x` resolves --root to <cwd>/--artifacts-dir and the ensureArtifactsDir leg then recursively creates that nonsense directory under the caller's cwd instead of failing with a usage error.
findings.impact: Malformed argv degrades silently rather than failing loudly: runDistCommand/runDistCommandInline resolve the flag-shaped token into an absolute path (resolve(getFlag(commandArgs, '--root') ?? '.')), setFlag overwrites the forwarded value with it, and mkdir(artifactsDir, { recursive: true }) materializes a directory literally named '--artifacts-dir' (or '--root') in the caller's cwd before dist ever runs - leaving stray state and an error from dist that points at the wrong cause. A token starting with '-' in value position should be rejected with a usage message; severity is low because it requires the user to omit the value and the damage is a stray directory plus a confusing error, not data loss.

The one normalization applied (stripping the leading slash before the drive letter) shows the author already had to handle URL-pathification side effects; decodeURIComponent before the regex is the missing half.

findings.title: INV-WH window-hide guard misses namespace, default, and dynamic child_process imports
findings.summary: The INV-WH detector only recognizes named brace imports from child_process, and its call-site regex deliberately excludes member calls, so a script using a namespace import, a default import, or await import('node:child_process') can spawn without windowsHide and pass both legs of the guard, silently reintroducing the win32 console-window flash the invariant exists to prevent.
findings.impact: A new spawning script written in any import form other than named-brace is never scanned (importsRawChildProcessSpawn returns false and the file is skipped before the windowsHide check), so the guarantee 'every spawn hides the window' is narrower than INV-WH's stated reach.
evidence: The import matcher is /import\s*\{([^}]*)\}\s*from\s*["'](?:node:)?child_process["']/g (line 305): it matches only the named-brace form. 'import * as cp from ...', 'import cp from ...', and dynamic 'await import("node:child_process")' never match.
rawCallRegex builds (?<![.\w$])callee\s*\( (line 317), so member calls such as cp.spawn( or cp.execSync( are excluded from the call-site scan even if the file were scanned.
Net effect: the two legs are complementary only for the named-import style; the namespace/default/dynamic styles evade both simultaneously.

The surrounding comment hardens the specifier forms ('Never narrow this back to one specifier') but does not state this remaining uncovered half, unlike other guards in the suite that state their residuals outright.

findings.title: Package-script reference regex consumes its boundary character, dropping every second adjacent file reference
findings.summary: The leading and trailing boundary classes in PACKAGE_SCRIPT_REFERENCE_PATTERN are consuming groups, so when one command string contains two file references separated by a single delimiter (e.g. "cat dist/a.js dist/b.js > out.js" or "node x.js y.js"), the first match swallows the shared delimiting space and matchAll cannot rematch the second token, silently omitting the package-script-link edge.

extractPackageScriptEdges iterates packageScriptCandidates(content) via matchAll, which resumes at lastIndex after the consumed delimiter; at that position the required leading [\s"'`] is no longer available, so the second token never matches.

findings.title: upsertManagedBlock appends a duplicate managed block when the begin marker exists without the end marker, and never converges
findings.summary: The managed-block pattern requires both INSTALL_MARKER_START and INSTALL_MARKER_END; an AGENTS.md or .github/copilot-instructions.md truncated or hand-edited to keep the begin marker but lose the end marker fails the replace branch and falls through to the append branch, so every install adds another full ## /remediate-code directive block and the file grows without bound.

writeManagedMarkdown (lines 135-145) is called on every install for AGENTS.md and copilot-instructions.md (writeCoreInstallAssets compatibilityBlockTargets), so each repeated install appends another copy.

findings.title: upsertManagedBlock passes replacement content as a String.replace pattern, so $ sequences would corrupt managed markdown; only the first duplicate block is refreshed
findings.summary: normalized.replace(blockPattern, blockContent) interprets '$&', "$'", '$`', '$$' in blockContent, and the non-greedy pattern replaces only the first managed block, leaving any duplicated block stale.
findings.impact: Today the only block content (buildInstallDirective) contains no '$', so behavior is correct; but writeManagedMarkdown/upsertManagedBlock is the generic managed-block writer for AGENTS.md and .github/copilot-instructions.md. Any future directive text containing a '$' sequence is silently rewritten by replace-pattern semantics (e.g. '$&' expands to the whole old block), corrupting the user's instructions file. Separately, if a file ever holds two begin/end marker pairs (hand-edit or past bug), only the first is updated and the duplicate survives every install, and the legacy/verify checks keep passing on the stale copy.
evidence: Replacement is a plain string argument to replace(), not a function, so MDN-defined $-substitution patterns apply.
blockPattern is non-greedy ([\s\S]*?) with no /g flag, so at most one block is replaced per call.

findings.title: Direct-invocation guard relies on the win32-broken hand-built file:// comparison plus a loose basename fallback
findings.summary: check-doc-links.mjs decides whether to run as a CLI via import.meta.url === `file://${process.argv[1]}` — the exact construct sibling gates document as broken on Windows drive letters — kept alive only by an endsWith basename fallback that fires on any argv[1] ending in the script name.
findings.impact: check-version-gates.mjs (lines 340-342) documents that a hand-built file:// + argv[1] string does not match import.meta.url on win32 because drive letters get one slash instead of three, and standardizes on pathToFileURL. This gate still uses the hand-built form as its primary test; on Windows the equality is effectively always false and execution depends wholly on the second clause, process.argv[1]?.endsWith("check-doc-links.mjs"), which also matches unrelated entry scripts whose filename merely ends with that suffix and bypasses the identity check the first clause was meant to provide. Every other script in this set uses the pathToFileURL comparison; this one diverges for no stated reason.
evidence: scripts/check-version-gates.mjs lines 340-343: 'win32: a hand-built `file://` + argv[1] string does not match import.meta.url (drive letters get one slash instead of three) ... pathToFileURL is the platform-agnostic comparison.'
scripts/check-backlog-budget.mjs line 355, scripts/check-backlog-line-numbers.mjs line 148, scripts/check-nightly-routine-prompt.mjs line 131 all use the pathToFileURL(...).href form.
runtime:unit:scripts: confirmed — Deterministic runtime command succeeded: npm test

findings.title: Direct-invocation probe can diverge from import.meta.url and silently skip the whole gate
findings.summary: main() runs only when pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href equals import.meta.url; argv[1] keeps the path as invoked while import.meta.url reflects Node's module resolution, so launching through a symlink/junction or a shim that rewrites the path makes the equality false and the script exits 0 having reconciled nothing.
evidence: A silent no-op of a release gate is indistinguishable from a pass: the mismatch case produces no output and a zero exit code
Normal npm-script invocation keeps the two in agreement, so the exposure is limited to symlinked/junctioned or shimmed launch paths

findings.title: Directory digest orders entries with localeCompare, making the hash environment-dependent
findings.summary: hashDirectory sorts dirents with localeCompare before folding them into the content hash, so identical directory contents can yield different digests under different ICU/locale environments; a codepoint comparison would make the digest depend on bytes only.
findings.impact: An affected-file entry naming a directory can flip from clean to changed (phantom staleness / spurious remediation re-work) when the artifact set is consumed in a process whose locale collation differs from the one that produced the baseline, contradicting the project's stable-content-derived-ordering invariant.
evidence: localeCompare output depends on the runtime ICU/locale data, not just the compared strings; the digest concatenates names in this order (parts.push(toDisplayRelativePath(...))) so ordering changes change the hash.
Every other ordering-sensitive hash path in the package relies on byte/path-derived order for exactly this reason.

findings.title: Disposition classifier order lets the generic doc rule shadow the specific install/examples rules
findings.summary: In inferDisposition, isDocPath (any '*.md' or a 'docs' segment) is checked BEFORE isGeneratedInstallArtifactPath and isExamplesOrFixturesPath, so '.audit-code/install/README.md' is recorded doc_only/'Documentation artifact.' and 'examples/x/README.md' never reaches its dedicated fixtures reason; the specific rules are only reachable for non-doc extensions, a coupling that is invisible at each rule's definition and changes recorded status/reason whenever rule order is reordered.
findings.impact: Scope outcome happens to be unchanged (both statuses are audit-excluded), but the persisted disposition records a wrong provenance reason, and any consumer branching on generated-vs-doc_only diverges; adding or moving a general rule can silently disable a specific one with no test signal.

findings.title: Document-intake seeding block duplicated inline across four dispatch tests despite the harness helper
findings.summary: Four tests in next-step-pipeline-dispatch.test.ts each hand-write the identical source-manifest/intake-summary/remediation-brief triple (~35 lines each) even though the same file destructures writeReadyStructuredAuditIntake from the harness and uses it elsewhere, so any intake-summary schema addition must be edited in four-plus inline copies.

affected_files.quoted_text: const { REPO_DIR, ARTIFACTS_DIR, saveState, acknowledgeResume, writeIntentCheckpoint, writeReadyStructuredAuditIntake, approveReviewGate, writeCompleteContractPipelineDag } = harness;

findings.impact: Drift risk: the inline copies already vary subtly (some pass label on sources, some omit affected_files entries, source_type "documents" vs "structured_audit"), so a future required intake-summary field fixed via the helper will leave these four tests silently pinning the old shape until they fail confusingly far from the cause.
evidence: Near-identical intake seeding blocks appear at lines 56-98, 100-152, 154-215, and 217-272 (same three writeFile calls differing only in goals text), while writeReadyStructuredAuditIntake is imported and used at lines 471 and 645.

findings.title: Documented (line_start, id) anchor ordering is never asserted by any test
findings.summary: buildAnalyzerSignalAnchorIndex guarantees each path bucket is pre-sorted by (line_start, id) so rendered anchor order stays byte-identical to the pre-index per-path extraction, but every existing test feeds at most one signal per audited path, so no assertion ever observes the sort; a comparator regression would silently reorder analyzer-signal anchors in dispatch packets without a red test.
evidence: Module comment states the invariant: "each bucket is pre-sorted by (line_start, id), matching the original per-path ordering".

tests/audit/file-anchors.test.ts asserts counts only ("analyzer_signals count must be 1 (only the matching path)"); its second fixture places rule-1 and rule-2 on DIFFERENT paths (src/counts.ts vs src/other.ts), so cross-signal order within one bucket is never produced, let alone checked.
runtime:unit:src-audit: confirmed — Deterministic runtime command succeeded: npm test
reproduction: Change the sort comparator to compare only a.id.localeCompare(b.id) (drop the line_start term).
Run the audit suite - no test fails, because no fixture puts two signals on the same path.

findings.title: First-write-wins baseline is a check-then-rename race; a concurrent duplicate registration can replace the baseline
findings.summary: Two processes registering the same session_id concurrently both pass existsSync and both rename, so last-writer-wins can refresh the stored baseline contrary to the documented first-write-wins guarantee; the failure direction is gate over-firing, not silence.
findings.impact: The documented invariant (comment block at lines 126-131: a resume re-fire must NOT refresh the baseline) holds only when writers are serialized. If two SessionStart firings with the same id interleave between the existsSync check and the rename, the second rename silently replaces the record, resetting baseline to the newer capture; work created between the two captures is then misclassified as foreign. Verified direction: the resulting misclassification makes closeout/friction gates fire MORE (whole-tree suspicion), never less, so this cannot silence the owner - it costs false positives in a narrow interleaving window. Mechanical fix is an exclusive-create (O_EXCL) on the final path or rename that refuses an existing target, keeping the skip-and-refresh branch as the only resume path.
evidence: Guard and mutation are separate statements: existsSync(finalPath) at line 138, then mkdir/write/rename at lines 147-150 with no lock or exclusive flag spanning them.
Node's rename replaces an existing destination on POSIX and Windows alike, so the loser's rename still lands rather than failing closed.
Every other store in the package routes writes through LockedJsonStore; this registry path performs its read-modify-write unlocked.

findings.title: Out-of-enum item statuses are silently answered false by every predicate via the as-cast plus nullish default
findings.summary: Each exported predicate takes a plain string, casts it with 'status as RemediationItemStatus', and defaults the lookup to false, so a status value outside ITEM_STATUSES (hand-edited state.json, or a state file written by a different version of the enum) is classified false by isInProgressStatus, isTerminalStatus, isSkipStatus and isUnsuccessfulEndStatus alike: the item reads as neither mid-flight nor terminal nor skipped nor unsuccessful, and statusToDisposition quietly turns it into an 'abandoned' coverage disposition instead of failing loudly.
findings.impact: A persisted unknown status produces contradictory classifications downstream rather than an error: callers gating on not-isTerminalStatus (for example dispatch eligibility and the validation artifact checks) see the item as actionable/non-finished, while the close phase sees it as non-terminal and force-closes it through the abandoned mapping, erasing whatever the unknown value meant. The blast radius stays small because the enum is compiled into the same package that writes the state file, so the value only arises from external edits or cross-version state.
evidence: isTerminalStatus (line 191) repeats the identical shape: TERMINAL_STATUS[status as RemediationItemStatus] ?? false;
isSkipStatus (line 210) and isUnsuccessfulEndStatus (line 228) use the same cast-plus-default pattern over SKIP_STATUS and UNSUCCESSFUL_END_STATUS.
statusToDisposition (line 262) defaults to the literal 'abandoned', so an unrecognized status also silently becomes an abandoned coverage disposition rather than surfacing.

The INV-ISC-1 header comment (lines 57-62) claims the exhaustive Records turn a status mistake into a compile error, but that guarantee holds only for in-enum additions; the exported API surface accepts arbitrary strings and swallows them, so the enforcement stops at the type boundary the cast deliberately crosses.

Narrowing check performed: the claimed mutual exclusivity and joint exhaustiveness of the four predicates DOES hold for all twelve in-enum statuses (pending through verified score in-progress only; resolved and resolved_no_change score verified-complete only; blocked and needs_clarification and abandoned score unsuccessful-end only; deemed_inappropriate and ignored score skip only), so any broader version of this concern stands only for out-of-enum inputs.
runtime:unit:src-remediate: confirmed — Deterministic runtime command succeeded: npm test
reproduction: Write a remediation state.json whose item status is a value absent from ITEM_STATUSES, for example a typo such as 'resloved' or a member removed by an older release.
Observe that isInProgressStatus, isTerminalStatus, isSkipStatus and isUnsuccessfulEndStatus all return false for it, and statusToDisposition returns 'abandoned', with no error raised anywhere.

findings.summary: The anchor array persisted in FileAnchorSummary (and merged route edges persisted in graph_bundle) is ordered with String.localeCompare, whose output varies with ICU locale/platform, so identical inputs can serialize to different bytes on different machines - churning the artifact content hash and cascading phantom staleness down the dependency DAG, against the repo invariant that extractor array order be a stable content-derived key.
findings.impact: localeCompare delegates to the ICU collator: Node built with full-icu orders by the ambient locale, small-icu builds fall back differently, and case/punctuation/diacritic weightings differ across platforms. Anchor names are extracted identifiers and route handlers are arbitrary source strings, so ties broken by these comparators can reorder between machines. Both outputs feed persisted artifacts (file-anchors packets, graph_bundle.json routes) whose content keys drive the staleness DAG per CLAUDE.md's stable-order rule ('ordered by a stable key derived from content ... never filesystem / readdir / iteration order' - the same hazard class, here introduced via locale sensitivity instead of iteration order). Replacing each localeCompare(a,b) with the plain relational comparison (a < b ? -1 : a > b ? 1 : 0) makes the order byte-stable code-point-wise with no behavioral loss for identifier/path strings. Scheduling-order uses of localeCompare (flowPlanning candidate sort, flowRequeue) are unaffected and need no change.
evidence: fileAnchors.ts buildFileAnchorSummary sorts the array that becomes persisted anchors via a.kind.localeCompare(b.kind) || a.name.localeCompare(b.name).

graphEnrichmentExecutor.ts mergeRoutes sorts the array written into graphs.routes via a.path.localeCompare(b.path) || a.handler.localeCompare(b.handler) || (a.method ?? '').localeCompare(b.method ?? '').

findings.title: runWrapperJsonOutput arms its timeout before child exists, so a synchronous spawn failure becomes a delayed TDZ crash

findings.title: The src tree is typechecked twice per gate run - check:tests is a strict superset of build, and the documented pre-push ritual pays tsc three times
findings.summary: verify:checks runs check:tests (tsc -p tsconfig.test.json, noEmit over src plus tests) and later build (tsc -p tsconfig.json, emit over src) in the same serial chain - the src tree is fully typechecked twice per run. The documented green-at-every-commit ritual (npm run build && npm run check) is worse: build already fails on any src type error, so the follow-up check (tsc over src with --noEmit) re-pays the same program and can only re-report what build just proved clean - and the two scripts exist as separate names (check, check:tests) whose superset relationship is implicit knowledge rather than stated. This is distinct from the banked parallelize-independent-verify-legs item: the improvement is eliminating a redundant leg, not overlapping independent ones. Fix: make one script the single type gate - check becomes an alias of the superset noEmit config (tsconfig.test.json) and check:tests is retired as a second name for the same thing - so the commit gate runs one typecheck and build's emit is the only src pass, removing both the double cost and the two-names-one-meaning drift surface.

findings.title: Hash-stability tie-break relies on locale-sensitive localeCompare, which is environment-dependent
findings.summary: The module's stated contract is that tie-breaking by request_id keeps the queue's content-derived order stable so the artifact hash cannot churn, but the comparison delegates to String.prototype.localeCompare with no explicit locale, whose collation is resolved from the host runtime's ICU - so two environments (different platforms, Node ICU builds, or ICU upgrades) can order equal-score requests differently, re-ordering the emitted queue and churning exactly the hash this function exists to keep stable.
findings.impact: A cross-platform or toolchain-upgrade run re-sorts tied entries differently than the run that produced a prior artifact, invalidating byte-stable comparisons of clarification-queue artifacts and contradicting both this file's own determinism comment and the extractor-ordering invariant it cites.
evidence: Line 29's own rationale pins the stake: "content-derived, never input order — an incidentally-ordered queue churns the artifact hash", yet localeCompare's outcome depends on the ambient locale rather than on content alone.
CLAUDE.md's platform-agnostic invariant requires core logic to avoid environment-dependent behavior; a default-locale collation call is such a dependency.
runtime:unit:src-audit: confirmed — Deterministic runtime command succeeded: npm test
reproduction: Build a CharterClarificationRequest[] where two entries share blast_radius+cascade_count and request_ids whose relative collation differs between codepoint order and ICU collation (e.g. differing case or embedded punctuation).
Run voiQueue under two Node builds with different ICU versions and compare the resulting arrays; any difference is a changed artifact payload for identical input.

findings.title: Live-release branch gate trusts release.target_commitish, which can be empty for tag-backed releases

findings.title: Session records and their pre-rename temp files are written with default permissions and a pid-embedding name
findings.summary: writeFileSync writes both the temp file and the final record with no mode, so the record - which carries the session id, registration source, and the full pre-session dirt baseline of file paths - inherits umask defaults, and the temp filename embeds process.pid, leaking both to any other local user who can read the directory on a POSIX shared host.
findings.impact: On a POSIX shared host, another user can read which files were dirty at session start and the pid of the registering process; low because the content is metadata, not secrets, and win32 is the primary platform.
evidence: writeFileSync(tmpPath, JSON.stringify(record, null, 2)) passes no mode option, so the file inherits umask defaults (typically 0o644 on POSIX; on win32 ACLs apply instead)
The record carries session_id, registered_at, source, and the full pre-session dirt baseline (paths), and the tmp name embeds process.pid
On win32, the primary platform, default ACLs restrict to the user, so this is a POSIX-shared-host concern only

findings.title: The --register CLI trusts CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR over cwd, so an inherited stale or hostile value registers into another checkout

themes.title: Synchronous child processes starve the liveness machinery the design depends on
themes.root_cause: Contract-assessment cluster: several hot paths spawn children synchronously (spawnSync, often with no timeout) while the advance holds the phase lock or runs on the single event loop. The staleness model judges locks by mtime refreshed by a setInterval heartbeat, which only fires while the loop runs, so any long synchronous child makes a LIVE holder look stale and stealable.
themes.suggested_fix_pattern: Make every child spawn asynchronous with a bounded timeout mapped into the existing degrade-to-status path, and move long-running work outside the lock behind the precomputed-verdict pattern the recovery verb already uses (src/remediate/steps/dispatch/hostHandoff.ts).

themes.title: Cross-invocation state persistence bypasses the atomic, locked house pattern
themes.root_cause: LockedJsonStore plus withFileLock is the declared substrate for guarded state, but sibling writers hand-roll weaker equivalents: a bare in-place writeFile inside lockedJsonMutate, plain unlocked read-modify-write over expected-submissions.json, and a stat-then-read window in the stale-lock steal that can adopt a fresh token. Each is a locally small deviation from a pattern whose whole point is crash and concurrency safety.
themes.suggested_fix_pattern: Route every guarded read-modify-write through LockedJsonStore (temp-plus-rename persistence, absent-vs-unreadable distinguished), and close the steal-side TOCTOU by reading the token under the same atomic claim that judges staleness.

themes.title: Gates and funnels exist but are not applied on every path that reaches them
themes.root_cause: Contract-assessment cluster: the repo builds the right predicates (admitSpawn consent veto, commandLeavesDeclaredShape, allowed_files re-check, the INV-RS-10 final gate) yet individual entry points skip them: closing-gate test/e2e spawns, resolved_no_change ingestion, non-git-root ingestion, cleanup --force, sample-run overwrites, consent for tree-mutating formatters, and the clarification-resolution transition straight to closing.
themes.suggested_fix_pattern: Funnel each operation class through its single existing chokepoint so skipping is impossible rather than discouraged, and state any uncovered half at the site the way triage.ts does, per the enforce-in-tooling invariant.

themes.title: Error paths resolve to the wrong outcome in both directions: silent success and unrecoverable throw
themes.root_cause: Swallowed reads, coerced fallbacks, and presence-only gates turn faults into success-shaped results (unparseable git status reads as a clean tree, a missing --results value no-ops green, a mistyped baseline gates against a phantom 0 percent, a crashed analyzer scan reports as findings), while the opposite defect throws past every gate where a structured refusal was expected, wedging subsequent steps.
themes.suggested_fix_pattern: Adopt the module's own stated direction (faults must over-fire, never silence): distinguish absent from unreadable, validate input shape before coercion, and replace post-gate throws with typed refusal values the frontier can drain.

themes.title: Drops and degenerations happen correctly but are recorded unfaithfully
themes.root_cause: Several stages collapse distinct causes into one undifferentiated outcome: checkpoint filter drops carry no reason, cap-tripped suite edges vanish without a marker, integrity checks cannot separate nothing-checked from all-clean, telemetry keys off prose prefixes, and summary counters are hardcoded to zero, so operators cannot audit what the tool actually did.
themes.suggested_fix_pattern: Give every drop, skip, and suppression a machine-readable reason field in the artifact it is already recorded in, and key events on identifiers rather than message wording; report examined-counts alongside clean-verdicts.

themes.title: Two coexisting declarations of one contract, with no mechanism forcing them to agree
themes.root_cause: Published JSON schemas disagree with the zod validator of record and the dispatch contract; a projection omits a field a consumer reads; templates and charter docs describe checks the named code does not implement; the wrapper envelope schema is imported by nothing. Each side was correct when written; nothing regenerates or verifies one from the other.
themes.suggested_fix_pattern: Single-source each contract and generate the derived copy (schema from zod, render from registry, template from emitted response shape), or add a conformance check to verify:checks that fails when the copies diverge.

themes.title: Correctness properties rest on convention and memory instead of mechanism
themes.root_cause: Artifact identity depends on every extractor remembering stable array order; DAG acyclicity is assumed, never asserted; guard allowlists exempt whole files; and the single-sourced identity and command-shape schemes have zero direct tests, so the property survives only as long as nobody touches its surroundings.
themes.suggested_fix_pattern: Move each property into the tool that can guarantee it: hash the stable projection at the single chokepoint, assert acyclicity where the map is defined, shrink allowlists to line-scoped exemptions, and pin the shared schemes with direct contract tests.

themes.title: Free-text strings doing structural work corrupt data silently
themes.root_cause: Space-delimited pair keys, comma-splitting a prose reason field, brace-blind regexes over route objects, and argv arrays re-parsed through a shell all encode structure in delimited text; when real-world content contains the delimiter, edges are misattributed, partitions gain phantom nodes, routes lose prefixes, and commands execute tokens that were never intended.
themes.suggested_fix_pattern: Replace joined-string keys with structured tuples or escaped encodings, model commands as argv end-to-end with shell interpretation refused at the boundary, and treat optional prose fields as provenance only, never as a grammar.

themes.title: Copy-paste accretion, already drifted, now causes actual data loss
themes.root_cause: The dedupe comparison exists eight-plus times across modules; sameLensDedupe's private copy lacks the mid-scan absorbed-guard the shared crossLens pass enforces, and that missing guard silently discards findings. The same ratchet produced near-identical wrapper pairs outside the jscpd scan, a comparator declared eight times, and multi-thousand-line modules carrying six unrelated responsibilities.
themes.suggested_fix_pattern: Delete the copies and import the single canonical implementation (this also fixes the data-loss bug for free), extend the duplication ratchet to cover wrapper/, and split the accreted modules along the subsystem seams their own comments already name.

themes.title: Test suite pins the wrong things: assertions that cannot fail and safety code with no coverage
themes.root_cause: A large class of findings shows green coverage that verifies nothing: fixtures lacking the very condition named (no cycle in the cyclic-seam test), assertions wrapped in may-not-fire guards, self-referential literal checks, as-never mutes, and suites coupled to live repo prose, alongside single-sourced safety mechanisms (ledger validation, anchor provenance, clause identity, build locks, ingest merges) that no test executes directly.
themes.suggested_fix_pattern: Repair vacuous tests by asserting the discriminating observable (the cycle exists, the failure_context appears, the spy counted), delete tested-but-unwired symbols, and give each declared single-source scheme a direct contract test so regression fails loudly.

themes.title: Conceptual design critique (kept distinct from contract assessment): standing decisions the shipped structure contradicts
themes.root_cause: These are not localized defects but critiques of direction: one-core-two-draws is unrealized at the largest shared seam; the bounded-step invariant is enforced three different ways with the harshest variant on remediate; the two-tier buy-versus-build policy has no enforcement while being crossed; expected:false perspective lanes sit wholly outside the fail-closed acceptance seam; auto-fix reorders consent after mutation; and the lock contradicts the policy bullet that would classify it. Each names a better architecture, not just a bug.
themes.suggested_fix_pattern: Decide the principle once at the owning altitude, then let structure enforce it: extract a parameterized shared workload/result core, state the bounded-call bound in the engine, declare a buy-class register with a red-build check, add a well-formedness gate at judge-ingest, and sequence auto-fix behind the confirmed intent checkpoint with a dry-run preview.

themes.title: The published artifact behaves differently from the developer checkout
themes.root_cause: Capabilities exercised in-repo depend on devDependencies a consumer never receives, a missing required host asset deploys nothing yet exits zero, and equals-form CLI flags are silently overridden by appended wrapper defaults, so what ships is quietly weaker than what was verified.
themes.suggested_fix_pattern: Move parser runtimes to optionalDependencies so the graded path engages by default, make required-asset absence a hard install failure, and parse flags positionally so user-supplied values win over appended defaults; surface degradation counts in the run summary.

executive_summary: The deterministic audit finalized 2,712 findings across 1,590 work blocks, dominated by five recurring root causes: synchronous child processes starving the mtime-heartbeat lock design, gates and predicates that exist but are skipped on specific entry points, error handling that resolves faults to success-shaped results (or unrecoverable throws), extensive copy-paste accretion whose drift now silently drops findings, and a very large test-validity class of assertions that cannot fail plus single-sourced safety mechanisms with no direct coverage. Conceptual design critiques are reported as their own theme rather than flattened into architecture: one-core-two-draws unrealized at the host-handoff seam, the bounded-call invariant triplicated, the buy-versus-build policy unenforced, and consent sequenced after tree mutation. Highest-leverage fixes are mechanical and shared: async bounded spawns, chokepoint routing for destructive operations, generated-or-verified contract copies, and deleting duplicated algorithm bodies in favor of the guarded canonical ones.
top_risks: Live-lock theft on remediation state: closing-gate suites and normal-lane required-test reruns run synchronously inside the phase lock, starving the heartbeat so a concurrent acquirer steals a LIVE lock and mutates state.json mid-run (ARC-305e7ec5, SEC-6377cd3f, DAT-f3d81e3f-2).

Arbitrary-scope destruction with no guard: cleanup --force deletes any resolved path including the working tree, sample-run overwrites a genuine audit bundle with fabricated state, and phase-1 auto-fix reformats uncommitted user work roughly nine obligations before the operator confirms anything (COR-e815b429, COR-34018c74, ARC-2d5421de).

Write-scope guarantee collapses to host attestation: resolved_no_change decisions and landed results on non-git roots are accepted with no corroboration, letting out-of-scope edits count as resolved and never enter applied_edit_surface (SEC-00c31ecc, SEC-d142de22).

Silent data loss in core algorithms: sameLensDedupe's missing absorbed-guard permanently drops findings unioned into an absorbed survivor, and space-containing paths fabricate phantom nodes and lose real coupling edges in the decomposition graph (COR-7a36066f, COR-4db6ff5a).

Declared-command-shape differential execution: test_command strings that the triage gate and handoff builder refuse as out-of-contract execute verbatim through shell:true when the same run reaches closing (SEC-305e7ec5).

Fail-open gates hide real work and real damage: unparseable git status reads as a clean tree, missing required host assets deploy nothing yet exit zero, and packaged installs silently lose the Tier-S parsers so audits ship materially weaker graphs with no signal (REL-4742dfbb, CFG-eefa6f69, CFG-eaffc6ab).
